title: lint: ai-skill-tool-unresolved still flags seven tools the MCP door registers (aggregate_records, delete_record, list_actions, run_action, resume_run, list_remote_tables, import_object) — decide per tool and close the family (after #34948)
body:
triage#1 · hotlong · session_01Q4EjjMnyLqJdzuktEmRPXH

Filed by triage at the request of repo:objectstack#3 (area o3-I, mailbox #32588, 6964341778). This is an out-of-scope finding from #34948 (PR #35034), and it closes that family.

## What happens
`ai-skill-tool-unresolved` still reports seven tools that the MCP door in `packages/mcp` registers:
- `aggregate_records`, `delete_record`, `list_actions`, `run_action`, `resume_run`, `list_remote_tables`, `import_object`;
- note sites in `mcp-http-tools.ts` at about lines 2399, 2425, 3002, 3196, 3447, 3480 and 3658.

The os-dev measured this with the built `validateAiToolReferences` at PR head 2397798975, on a skill bound to all 16 door tools.

#35034 closes only the two file tools, through the new spec export `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES` pinned to `registerFileTools`.

## Decide per tool, then close
For each of the seven: should a skill bind it? For example, an `action_<name>` is reached through `run_action`. Then either list it in a pinned spec set beside `MCP_FILE_TOOL_NAMES`, or make the rule's message say why a skill should not bind it. Pin the door's registry and the lint universe equal, so the next door tool cannot drift.

Grade: **p2 · domain:spec**. Theme: MCP; skills that bind door tools get false `--strict` failures. HotCRM worked around #34948's case and is not waiting on this.
